findings.title: Configured Shamir threshold reaches the server but not the production client processor.
findings.scope_basis: Explicit additional ownership includes MPC client/server strategies; reconstruction, threshold wiring, and numerical correctness were claimed as reviewed. This is an existing advertised configuration, not a new feature request.
findings.description: MPCLifecycleStrategy only supplies client_id, round_store, and debug_artifacts. With five selected clients and server.mpc_shamir_threshold=1, the registry-created client processors use their default threshold 3 while the aggregation strategy reconstructs using threshold 1. A degree-two polynomial evaluated at the client coordinate is mistaken for its constant term, silently biasing valid model weights. Tests that manually pass the same threshold to both ends miss this production wiring gap.

steps: Use configure_environment with clients.outbound_processors=[mpc_model_encrypt_shamir], five selected clients and server.mpc_shamir_threshold=1.
Initialize a real isolated RoundInfoStore for round 9 and record one sample for each selected client.
Build actual MPCLifecycleStrategy kwargs and registry.get(Client) outbound pipelines; process identical float64 weights [0.125,-0.2] for all five clients.
Aggregate actual shares with MPCShamirAggregationStrategy using the configured server threshold, preserving ordinary sender-target orientation.

findings.correction: Propagate the existing server.mpc_shamir_threshold consistently into registry-created Shamir client processor kwargs, with a defined precedence for explicitly supplied processor kwargs. Keep the current real-valued/scaled prototype and default threshold behavior.
findings.acceptance: A config-driven client lifecycle/registry plus real store/aggregation probe with a nondefault threshold below n-2 must match the independent weighted plaintext reference; default and zero-count behavior remain correct.

findings.title: QSGD produces infinities from valid finite float32 values because scaling overflows before division.
findings.scope_basis: Accepted QSGD finite values, error bounds, and malformed-input behavior are part of the additional processor correctness fixes.
findings.description: The header scale and quantized codes pass all new finite/length/level checks, but zeta * max_v / tuning_param multiplies in float32 before normalization. At level 64, the code 63 times a finite scale 1e38 overflows even though the final reconstructed endpoint should be 1e38. The decoder silently returns infinities and breaks its finite/error-bound contract.

reproduction.minimal_python:
x = torch.tensor([1e38, -1e38, 0.], dtype=torch.float32)
encoded = model_quantize_qsgd.Processor(client_id=1).process({'w': x})
y = model_dequantize_qsgd.Processor(client_id=1).process(encoded)['w']

findings.correction: Normalize codes before multiplying by the scale, or use a sufficiently wide intermediate and cast only the final result. Preserve the existing sign/magnitude wire, levels, and max-norm stochastic quantization equation.
findings.acceptance: Roundtrip valid large finite positive/negative float32 endpoints at the default level with finite results and the existing error bound, alongside the already passing ordinary/zero/empty cases.

findings.title: Valid Unicode outside the BMP is emitted as invalid TOML surrogate escapes.
findings.scope_basis: Unicode key and nested array-table roundtrips are expressly included in the TOML repair and acceptance review.
findings.description: Quoted keys and string values use json.dumps with ensure_ascii=True. Non-BMP code points become two surrogate \u escapes. JSON permits that representation, but TOML requires Unicode scalar values and rejects the generated document. BMP examples pass while valid emoji and supplementary CJK text fail.

reproduction.actual_error: TOMLDecodeError: Escaped character is not a Unicode scalar value (at line 1, column 8)
reproduction.independent_reference: Each valid input mapping must be reproduced exactly by stdlib tomllib.

findings.correction: Emit these code points as actual UTF-8 characters (for example ensure_ascii=False) or valid eight-digit TOML Unicode escapes in both keys and values. Preserve the existing mixed-array/null wrapper conventions.
findings.acceptance: Stdlib tomllib roundtrips a non-BMP quoted key, ordinary string value, and nested array-table key, while the existing literal-dot/BMP/comment structure remains correct.

findings.title: The accepted threshold-1000 boundary can enter an impossible unbounded coefficient-selection loop.
findings.scope_basis: The revised processor explicitly accepts thresholds through min(participants,1000) and claims bounded exact-range rejection instead of inaccurate prototype results.
findings.description: A scaled secret in 1..999 already occupies one element of the finite random coefficient pool. Threshold 1000 requires 999 more distinct coefficients, but only 998 remain. The while value in coefficients loop therefore cannot terminate. The later coordinate-range error is never reached. This concerns the currently accepted boundary; rejecting unsupported input promptly is sufficient and does not require a new cryptographic scheme.

reproduction.actual: Isolated process printed entered and failed to return within the 4-second subprocess deadline; the process was contained by the review harness.
reproduction.independent_reason: The scaled secret is 10. The pool 1..999 excluding 10 contains 998 values, strictly fewer than the 999 additional coefficients required.
reproduction.public_path: Processor.process accepts this threshold at line 125 and invokes _split_tensor -> _secret_shares for a scaled model element of 0.000010.

findings.correction: Validate coefficient-pool capacity before sampling and reject impossible requests, or use bounded sampling without replacement with an explicit capacity check. Preserve the real-valued polynomial prototype; no finite-field redesign is needed.
findings.acceptance: The currently accepted impossible boundary fails promptly with a useful error before any shares are persisted; normal thresholds retain the existing numerical reconstruction reference.
